title: Sandboxable Recommendation Cards with Temporal Diff and Immutable Apply Ledger
creator: Asha Kapoor
description: Introduce an interactive recommendation card pattern in Optimize that users can sandbox (dry-run) changes, preview token-level cost deltas across time windows, and apply changes through a ledger-backed operation that supports canary deploys and automatic rollback. The goal is to make batching/caching/quantization recommendations actionable while guaranteeing a full, auditable history for compliance and post-mortem analysis.
acceptance_criteria: Recommendation cards display estimated monthly and 7-day token savings, confidence band, and sample workload examples.
Users can open a 'Temporal Diff' preview that shows before/after per-route token and latency distribution across selectable time ranges (7d/30d/90d).
A Sandbox (dry-run) mode simulates the configuration change and surfaces any incompatibilities or potential QoS regressions without touching production routes.
Apply flow supports canary % rollout with automatic rollback policies if error rate or latency regressions exceed thresholds.
Every apply (including dry-run) is recorded in an immutable audit ledger with operator, diffs, timestamp, and linked artifacts (PR, runbook).
Console exposes an 'Apply History' view with filters (route, model, user, status) and a one-click rollback to the previous safe configuration.
Design & engineering sign-off on the accessibility and keyboard-first interactions for the card and diff views.
Backend exposes endpoints for diff computation and sandbox validation that meet SLOs for interactive UX (<2s for most cards).
comments: 2026-02-27 — Asha Kapoor: Created ticket after customer research with two enterprise accounts that delayed applies due to lack of auditable sandboxing. Proposed: card-centric workflow where each recommendation is its own revisionable object.

2026-03-02 — Miguel Santos: Drafted initial UX flow; attached Figma frame for cards + temporal diff. Key trade-off: expensive diff calcs for 90d windows vs responsive UX. Proposal: lazy compute for 90d and cached precomputes for active customers.
2026-03-05 — Design review (DES-10112): Feedback to reduce cognitive load—remove raw token counts from primary card, surface percentage and dollar estimates; keep raw counts in expanded diff.

2026-03-07 — Eng sync (ENG-34122): Runtime team can provide sampled telemetry and delta estimation API; need to add a background job for prefix/KV cache impact estimation. Engineering raised concern about SLO for diff endpoint—agreed on 2s target for 7d/30d, 6s for 90d lazy path.
2026-03-10 — Security: must include KMS audit annotations for any apply that touches private deployments. Added security_review_required flag.
2026-03-12 — PM review: Added canary rollout UI pattern and automatic rollback triggers. Decided to allow customers to pin a rollback window (default 30 minutes).
2026-03-14 — Implementation note (Miguel): Backend PR opened: https://github.com/redwood-inference/optimize/pull/428. Waiting on infra for cache precompute job (ENG-34700).
2026-03-14 — Next steps: Finalize Figma prototypes, complete backend diff API contract, schedule design handoff, and draft QA plan with acceptance tests and load tests for diff endpoints.
